newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast light crudes rise, lack of deals.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast light crudes rise, lack of deals.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes rose with WTI/Cushing prices in a Wednesday session that lacked sales, trade sources said.
Alaska North Slope (ANS) differentials stayed flat at $1.10 a barrel under March West Texas Intermediate.
BP, a key producer, continued to withhold an asking price for ANS, as they continued to evaluate their shipping capability, buyers said.
Outright prices for ANS rose 15 cents from Tuesday to 21.45/21.65 a barrel.
Kern River crude was assessed $14 53/14.73 a barrel, with bids firming after most price discussion rose above last week's $3 discount deal.
